policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads simply 'beyond the Jordan westward' with no ASV note attached to this unit. Both the qere בְּעֵבֶר ('on the other side of') and the ketiv מעבר ('from the other side of / beyond') are rendered by the same English 'beyond' in this locative phrase, and the ASV supplies no 'from' or other wording that would separate them. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
